notes.text: (1) Matthew xxiv. 44. (2) Luke xvi. 9. (3) Hebrews xiii. 14.

verses.text: Very quickly will there be an end of thee here; take heed therefore how it will be with thee in another world.
verses.modernizedText: Very quickly your life here will end; take heed, therefore, how it will be with you in another world.

verses.text: To-day man is, and to-morrow he will be seen no more.
verses.modernizedText: Today a person is here, and tomorrow he will be seen no more.

verses.text: And being removed out of sight, quickly also he is out of mind.
verses.modernizedText: And once removed from sight, he is quickly out of mind as well.

verses.text: O the dulness and hardness of man’s heart, which thinketh only of the present, and looketh not forward to the future.
verses.modernizedText: Oh, the dullness and hardness of the human heart, which thinks only of the present and does not look forward to the future.

verses.text: Thou oughtest in every deed and thought so to order thyself, as if thou wert to die this day.
verses.modernizedText: In every deed and thought you ought to order yourself as if you were to die today.

verses.text: If thou hadst a good conscience thou wouldst not greatly fear death.
verses.modernizedText: If you had a good conscience, you would not greatly fear death.

verses.text: It were better for thee to watch against sin, than to fly from death.
verses.modernizedText: It would be better for you to watch against sin than to flee from death.

verses.text: If to-day thou art not ready, how shalt thou be ready to-morrow?
verses.modernizedText: If you are not ready today, how will you be ready tomorrow?

verses.text: To-morrow is an uncertain day; and how knowest thou that thou shalt have a to-morrow?
verses.modernizedText: Tomorrow is uncertain; and how do you know that you will have a tomorrow?

verses.text: What doth it profit to live long, when we amend so little?
verses.modernizedText: What good is it to live long when we amend so little?

verses.text: Ah! long life doth not always amend, but often the more increaseth guilt.
verses.modernizedText: Ah! A long life does not always amend us, but often increases our guilt all the more.

verses.text: Oh that we might spend a single day in this world as it ought to be spent!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, that we might spend a single day in this world as it ought to be spent!

verses.text: Many there are who reckon the years since they were converted, and yet oftentimes how little is the fruit thereof.
verses.modernizedText: Many count the years since they were converted, and yet how little fruit there often is from them.

verses.text: If it is a fearful thing to die, it may be perchance a yet more fearful thing to live long.
verses.modernizedText: If it is fearful to die, it may perhaps be even more fearful to live long.

verses.text: Happy is the man who hath the hour of his death always before his eyes, and daily prepareth himself to die.
verses.modernizedText: Happy is the person who always has the hour of his death before his eyes and prepares himself daily to die.

verses.text: If thou hast ever seen one die, consider that thou also shalt pass away by the same road.
verses.modernizedText: If you have ever seen someone die, consider that you too will pass away by the same road.

verses.text: When it is morning reflect that it may be thou shalt not see the evening, and at eventide dare not to boast thyself of the morrow.
verses.modernizedText: When morning comes, reflect that perhaps you will not see the evening, and in the evening do not dare to boast of tomorrow.

verses.text: Always be thou prepared, and so live that death may never find thee unprepared.
verses.modernizedText: Always be prepared, and live so that death may never find you unprepared.

verses.text: Many die suddenly and unexpectedly.
verses.modernizedText: Many die suddenly and unexpectedly.

verses.text: For at such an hour as ye think not, the Son of Man cometh.(1) When that last hour shall come, thou wilt begin to think very differently of thy whole life past, and wilt mourn bitterly that thou hast been so negligent and slothful.
verses.modernizedText: For at an hour when you do not expect Him, the Son of Man comes.(1) When that last hour comes, you will begin to think very differently about your whole past life and will mourn bitterly that you have been so negligent and slothful.

verses.text: Happy and wise is he who now striveth to be such in life as he would fain be found in death!
verses.modernizedText: Happy and wise is the person who now strives to be in life what he would wish to be found in death!

verses.text: For a perfect contempt of the world, a fervent desire to excel in virtue, the love of discipline, the painfulness of repentance, readiness to obey, denial of self, submission to any adversity for love of Christ; these are the things which shall give great confidence of a happy death.
verses.modernizedText: For perfect contempt of the world, a fervent desire to excel in virtue, love of discipline, the pain of repentance, readiness to obey, denial of self, and submission to any adversity for love of Christ: these are the things that will give great confidence of a happy death.

verses.text: Whilst thou art in health thou hast many opportunities of good works; but when thou art in sickness I know not how much thou wilt be able to do.
verses.modernizedText: While you are healthy you have many opportunities for good works, but when you are sick I do not know how much you will be able to do.

verses.text: Few are made better by infirmity: even as they who wander much abroad seldom become holy.
verses.modernizedText: Few are made better by infirmity, just as those who wander much abroad seldom become holy.

verses.text: Trust not thy friends and kinsfolk, nor put off the work of thy salvation to the future, for men will forget thee sooner than thou thinkest.
verses.modernizedText: Do not trust your friends and relatives or put off the work of your salvation to the future, for people will forget you sooner than you think.

verses.text: It is better for thee now to provide in time, and to send some good before thee, than to trust to the help of others.
verses.modernizedText: It is better for you now to provide in time and send some good before you than to trust in the help of others.

verses.text: If thou art not anxious for thyself now, who, thinkest thou, will be anxious for thee afterwards?
verses.modernizedText: If you are not concerned for yourself now, who do you think will be concerned for you afterward?

verses.text: Now the time is most precious.
verses.modernizedText: Now the time is most precious.

verses.text: Now is the accepted time, now is the day of salvation.
verses.modernizedText: Now is the accepted time, now is the day of salvation.

verses.text: But alas! that thou spendest not well this time, wherein thou mightest lay up treasure which should profit thee everlastingly.
verses.modernizedText: But alas, you do not spend well this time in which you might lay up treasure that would benefit you everlastingly.

verses.text: The hour will come when thou shalt desire one day, yea, one hour, for amendment of life, and I know not whether thou shalt obtain.
verses.modernizedText: The hour will come when you will desire one day, indeed one hour, to amend your life, and I do not know whether you will obtain it.

verses.text: Oh, dearly beloved, from what danger thou mightest free thyself, from what great fear, if only thou wouldst always live in fear, and in expectation of death!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, dearly beloved, from what danger and what great fear you might free yourself if only you would always live in fear and in expectation of death!

verses.text: Strive now to live in such wise that in the hour of death thou mayest rather rejoice than fear.
verses.modernizedText: Strive now to live in such a way that in the hour of death you may rejoice rather than fear.

verses.text: Learn now to die to the world, so shalt thou begin to live with Christ.
verses.modernizedText: Learn now to die to the world, and so you will begin to live with Christ.

verses.text: Learn now to contemn all earthly things, and then mayest thou freely go unto Christ.
verses.modernizedText: Learn now to despise all earthly things, and then you may freely go to Christ.

verses.text: Keep under thy body by penitence, and then shalt thou be able to have a sure confidence.
verses.modernizedText: Keep your body under control by penitence, and then you will be able to have sure confidence.

verses.text: Ah, foolish one! why thinkest thou that thou shalt live long, when thou art not sure of a single day?
verses.modernizedText: Ah, foolish one! Why do you think you will live long when you are not sure of a single day?

verses.text: How many have been deceived, and suddenly have been snatched away from the body!
verses.modernizedText: How many have been deceived and suddenly snatched away from the body!

verses.text: How many times hast thou heard how one was slain by the sword, another was drowned, another falling from on high broke his neck, another died at the table, another whilst at play!
verses.modernizedText: How many times have you heard how one was slain by the sword, another drowned, another fell from a height and broke his neck, another died at the table, another while at play!

verses.text: One died by fire, another by the sword, another by the pestilence, another by the robber.
verses.modernizedText: One died by fire, another by the sword, another by pestilence, another by a robber.

verses.text: Thus cometh death to all, and the life of men swiftly passeth away like a shadow.
verses.modernizedText: Thus death comes to all, and human life swiftly passes away like a shadow.

verses.text: Who will remember thee after thy death?
verses.modernizedText: Who will remember you after your death?

verses.text: And who will entreat for thee?
verses.modernizedText: And who will plead for you?

verses.text: Work, work now, oh dearly beloved, work all that thou canst.
verses.modernizedText: Work, work now, oh dearly beloved, work all that you can.

verses.text: For thou knowest not when thou shalt die, nor what shall happen unto thee after death.
verses.modernizedText: For you do not know when you will die or what will happen to you after death.

verses.text: While thou hast time, lay up for thyself undying riches.
verses.modernizedText: While you have time, lay up undying riches for yourself.

verses.text: Think of nought but of thy salvation; care only for the things of God.
verses.modernizedText: Think of nothing but your salvation; care only for the things of God.

verses.text: Make to thyself friends, by venerating the saints of God and walking in their steps, that when thou failest, thou mayest be received into everlasting habitations.(2)
verses.modernizedText: Make friends for yourself by venerating the saints of God and walking in their steps, so that when you fail, you may be received into everlasting dwellings.(2)

verses.text: Keep thyself as a stranger and a pilgrim upon the earth, to whom the things of the world appertain not.
verses.modernizedText: Keep yourself as a stranger and a pilgrim on earth, to whom the things of the world do not belong.

verses.text: Keep thine heart free, and lifted up towards God, for here have we no continuing city.(3) To Him direct thy daily prayers with crying and tears, that thy spirit may be found worthy to pass happily after death unto its Lord.
verses.modernizedText: Keep your heart free and lifted up toward God, for here we have no continuing city.(3) Direct your daily prayers to Him with cries and tears, that your spirit may be found worthy to pass happily after death to its Lord.

verses.text: Amen.
verses.modernizedText: Amen.
